name: Pending authorized message on a gated run → spawn the intent classifier
description:
The classifier spawn (nl-conversation-intent group 4, design D3/D5). When handleMessage's NL bridge has stamped conversation.pending.{message-id,author,body} on a run at awaiting_approval (an AUTHORIZED, non-command, not-yet-classified message — the bridge already enforced all three), spawn ONE inherit-scoped role=conversation classifier loop to read that single message. The pending author + body are TEMPLATED onto the prompt from the run's own triples (a rule can only template the firing entity's triples — the reason the bridge stamps the message ON the run, design Context). The persona (configs/personas/fragments/conversation) carries the closed-taxonomy decision contract; classify_intent validates the intent against the same Go taxonomy and HARNESS-BINDS the message id + author from these pending triples, never from the model (H3).

ONE-AT-A-TIME SERIALIZATION (load-bearing for the grp2 ledger): the fire-once marker conversation.classifier.dispatched = the pending message id, stamped BEFORE the publish and guarded length_eq 0. While a classifier is in flight the marker blocks a second spawn, so at most ONE classifier loop runs per run — classify_intent's read→replace classified-ledger is safe ONLY under this invariant (OwnedFactWriter assumes one concurrent writer of a prefix). The marker VALUE is read by classify_intent as its READ-ONCE BINDING (grp4-review HIGH-1): the pending slot is latest-wins, so if a second authorized message replaces it during the model turn, the tool sees slot-id ≠ dispatched-id and FAULTS (no stamp, no ledger entry) rather than bind the new message's identity to a judgment of the old message's text; the faulted terminal flows the release + the group-5 fallback note. The marker also makes the spawn replay-safe (publish_agent is not idempotent; the run is a long-lived, replay-exposed entity — the dev.developer.dispatched precedent, dispatch-developer.json:12). The marker is RELEASED by 04-classifier-terminal-release on the loop terminal (pending cleared first, then the marker), which re-arms this rule for the NEXT authorized message — the ledger dedup in the bridge, not this marker, is what stops an already-classified message re-entering.

GATE-FACTS GUARDS (grp4-review M1): both run.change.approved and run.change.rejected must be ABSENT — the same cell the routing rules (03a/03b) require. A run still at awaiting_approval that already carries a gate fact (the D7 both-facts park; the publish→stamp window; a stamped-but-not-yet-resumed run) would spend a classifier turn whose intent can never route; these guards make that turn unspendable. Strictly narrowing: a genuinely open gate always has both absent.

FIRING-CAP OPT-OUT (grp4-review H1, load-bearing): both actions carry explicit max_iterations: 0. The engine's per-action firing cap DEFAULTS to 3 per rule+entity (DefaultActionMaxIterations, persisted in RULE_STATE) — and this is the repo's first rule designed to re-fire indefinitely on ONE entity (the run, one edge per pending→spawn→release cycle). Under the default cap the FOURTH authorized message of a run's gate lifetime would be silently skipped (pending stamped, no spawn, no fault, no note — the silent-dead-lane class). The spend stays bounded by the bridge's ledger dedup, this marker, and the release — that is their whole job; the cap added nothing but the dead lane.

RUN BINDING: run_scope=inherit reads the run's bare agent.loop.run anchor (stamped by 01-anchor-gated-run at gate entry) and binds the classifier's RunID to this run, so classify_intent resolves the run entity from its call metadata and stamps conversation.intent.* there (H2). The agent.loop.run ne "" condition is load-bearing: without the anchor present, inherit binds NO RunID and classify_intent faults on a missing run id.

TOOL SURFACE: tools advertises EXACTLY [classify_intent] (beta.149 executor enforcement makes the scoped list load-bearing at execution — the classifier can call nothing else) and tool_choice=required forces the call so a weak model cannot terminate text-only (D2). One model turn per DISTINCT authorized message (D9): the bridge's ledger dedup + this marker + the release rule bound the spend. G2: no lifecycle transition — the intent fact routes via 03a/03b and the deterministic apply consumer stamps the gate fact; a rule owns any transition.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.conversation
on_enter.prompt:
SEMDEV CONVERSATION READER — classify ONE human message on this run's approval thread.

This run is awaiting human approval of its proposed change. A collaborator has posted a message on the thread. Read it and record what they MEANT with the classify_intent tool: intent "approve" only for an unmistakable directive to proceed, "reject" only for an unmistakable directive to stop or abandon the change, and "none" for anything else — thanks, questions, reactions, ambiguous positivity, thinking-out-loud. Quote the words that decided you in reason. You classify meaning only: authorization, the author's identity, and every approval fact are the harness's job, never yours.

Message author: $entity.triple.conversation.pending.author
Message text:
$entity.triple.conversation.pending.body

metadata.station: classifier spawn — one inherit-scoped conversation loop per pending message (group 4, design D3/D5)
metadata.trigger_rationale: fires on the RUN (the pending message + phase + marker all live there; the bridge stamps pending on the run precisely so this rule can template it). The bridge already enforced authorized + non-command + not-in-ledger, so every fire is a distinct authorized message.
metadata.serialization_invariant: the conversation.classifier.dispatched marker (length_eq 0 guard, stamped BEFORE the publish) is the single-writer-per-run serialization classify_intent's read→replace ledger DEPENDS on — at most one classifier loop in flight per run. Its VALUE is the tool's read-once binding: classify_intent faults on slot-id ≠ dispatched-id (HIGH-1). Released by 04-classifier-terminal-release on the loop terminal; re-arms for the next message.
metadata.restart_safe: marker stamped before the (non-idempotent) publish. HONEST LIMITS (grp4-review M3/M4): the engine executes actions best-effort (a failed action logs actionFailuresTotal and CONTINUES) — a failed marker-add followed by a successful publish leaves an unmarked in-flight classifier, and a replay then double-spawns, degrading to the bounded consequence grp2's ledger comment names (a dropped ledger id → one re-classification, never a false approval). And a failed publish AFTER the marker stamp, or a classifier loop that wedges without ever stamping agent.loop.outcome, leaves the marker unreleased FOREVER: publish_agent is NOT a station dispatch (nothing stamps station.dispatch.failed; run-lifecycle/05/06 never fire), so the NL lane closes SILENTLY for that run — new messages stamp pending and die at this guard; the exact command is the recovery. Fail direction is safe (the gate stays closed). A marker-leak reconciliation is a named pre-production follow-up (tasks 7.1).
metadata.firing_cap: max_iterations: 0 on BOTH actions (grp4-review H1) — the engine's default per-action cap (3, per rule+entity, RULE_STATE-persisted) would silently kill the NL lane on the run's 4th authorized message. The marker + ledger + release bound the spend instead. Pinned by TestClassifierSpawnRuleContract.
metadata.run_binding: run_scope=inherit reads the run's bare agent.loop.run (01-anchor-gated-run). The ne "" condition serializes anchor-before-spawn across KV revisions — a pending stamp that races the anchor waits for the anchor's revision.
metadata.cost: one model turn per DISTINCT authorized non-command message on a still-open gate (D9): bridge ledger dedup upstream, this marker + the gate-facts guards in flight, terminal-release downstream.
